data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's distinguishing test requires perturbing checklist features and comparing panel degradation to a *hypothetical* single expert forced to use the same perturbed rule. But the question asks what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish genuine gain from compliance. A counterfactual expert that is not actually evaluated cannot supply observable evidence within that evaluation, so the proposed iff-criterion is not satisfiable by the evaluation alone; it smuggles in an unobserved baseline. Worse, the third countercondition (perfectly complete/lossless checklist) concedes the 'genuine vs. mere compliance' distinction may not exist, yet the claim is stated as a biconditional iff, so the criterion fails exactly when the question still demands a verdict.
